hero.title: Ashoka's Policy of Dhamma
hero.description: A socio-ethical code promulgated by Emperor Ashoka to foster social harmony, tolerance, and moral rectitude across the Mauryan Empire.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Critical phases in the evolution of Ashoka's religious and administrative policy.

cards.details: Kalinga War: The turning point. The horror of the war led Ashoka to embrace Buddhism and formulate his policy of Dhamma.
Inauguration of Dhamma-mahamattas: Ashoka appoints special officers to propagate Dhamma.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Useful triggers for UPSC Prelims recall.

items.title: S.A.D.D.A
items.decryption: Remember these as the core pillars of Ashoka's policy: Self-control (Atmasamyama), Ahimsa (Non-violence), Dhamma-mahamattas (officials), Duty (Dharma), and respect for elders/ancestors.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Mistaking Dhamma for Buddhism: Ashoka's Dhamma was a social code of conduct, not purely a theological Buddhist doctrine.
Assuming it was state-mandated religion: Ashoka practiced religious tolerance; Dhamma was meant for all sects (Brahmanas, Shramanas, etc.).

deepDive.description: Master the key concepts and dimensions of this topic.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Tenets

  • Ahimsa (Non-violence)
  • Religious Tolerance
  • Respect for Elders
  • Paternalistic Kingship

Administrative Tools

  • Dhamma-mahamattas
  • Rock Edicts
  • Pillar Edicts
  • Public welfare works
  • Key Components:
    • Social Harmony: Reducing conflict between religious sects.
    • Moral Discipline: Promotion of kindness, truthfulness, and purity.
    • Administrative Outreach: Dhamma-mahamattas served as bridge between the King and public welfare.
